title: Pharmaceuticals in Water: Sources, Fate and Effects (Rodriguez-Mozaz & Weinberg, Environmental Health Perspectives 2010)
source: Environmental Health Perspectives, 2010; assigned from the beginning up to the section “Best management practices”
lecture: Assigned for 10/9; discussed in class 10/13 with the discussion guide
about: A review of how medications reach ground water, surface water and drinking water and what is known about their effects. The body metabolizes only part of a prescribed drug, so unchanged drug and metabolites leave in human waste and travel through wastewater into streams, lakes and the water that drinking-water plants use (p. 1016). Wastewater treatment plants are the main point where these drugs enter surface water, because their treatment steps were not designed to remove pharmaceuticals; some drugs collect in biosolids sold as fertilizer; farm animals receive drugs directly in feed (p. 1017). People take the drugs in mainly by mouth through drinking water (p. 1018). The assigned portion stops before the best-management-practices section.

The dose contrast: human exposure far below a therapeutic dose; wildlife exposed continuously
